newsitem.title: FRANCE: French police seize six over Corsican bombs.
newsitem.headline: French police seize six over Corsican bombs.

text.p: French police detained six people on Wednesday suspected of ties to separatist bombings on the Mediterranean island of Corsica after guerrillas struck again with two blasts overnight.

Police said five men and a woman were seized in raids in the island's main town of Ajaccio after an investigation into night attacks on September 21-22 against post offices in Ajaccio, Cargese and Sagone.
Two other men have been in custody for a month on suspicion of involvement in the attacks.
The two overnight blasts destroyed a building owned by state-run France Telecom and another used by paramilitary gendarmerie police, officials said.
Four or five armed, hooded men broke into the telecommunications building in Ajaccio shortly after midnight, overpowered the security guard and planted a bomb.
Police said the building was reduced to rubble and a nearby car was crushed by a slab of concrete.

No one has so far claimed responsibility for the attack, or for the blast a few hours earlier in Porto-Vecchio in southern Corsica, where a bomb badly damaged a private villa which, in the summer, accommodates gendarmerie officers.
Prime Minister Alain Juppe, brushing aside separatist threats, pledged on Tuesday to crack down on the guerrillas' activities but conceded Paris faced a long haul to end bombings.
The government says 26 people have been placed in custody after a spate of attacks in recent months, even though many more had been freed after brief detention.
